questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a given air-cored solenoid is physically stretched so that its length doubles (keeping the total number of turns and cross-sectional area constant), its self-inductance remains unchanged.
Reason (R): The self-inductance of a long solenoid is directly proportional to the square of its turns per unit length and directly proportional to its length.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
The self-inductance of a solenoid in terms of total turns $N$ is given by $L = \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l}$.
When the solenoid is stretched to double its length ($l' = 2l$) while keeping $N$ and $A$ constant, the new self-inductance becomes $L' = \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{2l} = \dfrac{L}{2}$.
Thus, the self-inductance becomes half of its original value, making Assertion (A) false.

In terms of turns per unit length $n$ ($n = \dfrac{N}{l}$), the self-inductance is $L = \mu_0 n^2 A l$.
This shows that self-inductance is directly proportional to the square of the turns per unit length ($n^2$) and directly proportional to its length ($l$).
Therefore, Reason (R) is true.

Hence, Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal battery of emf $V$ is connected in series with a switch, a resistor of resistance $R$, and a network of three identical inductors (each of inductance $L$). The inductor network consists of two inductors connected in parallel, which are then connected in series with the third inductor. The switch is closed at $t=0$. Neglecting mutual inductance, what is the initial rate of change of current drawn from the battery immediately after the switch is closed?
questions.solution:
At $t=0$, immediately after the switch is closed, the current in the circuit is zero ($I = 0$).

The voltage drop across the resistor is $V_R = IR = 0$.

Therefore, the entire battery emf $V$ appears across the equivalent inductance of the network.

The equivalent inductance $L_{eq}$ of two inductors in parallel is $\dfrac{L}{2}$.

This combination is in series with the third inductor, so the total equivalent inductance is:
$L_{eq} = L + \dfrac{L}{2} = \dfrac{3L}{2}$

Using the relation $V = L_{eq} \dfrac{dI}{dt}$, the initial rate of change of current is:
$\dfrac{dI}{dt} = \dfrac{V}{L_{eq}} = \dfrac{V}{\dfrac{3L}{2}} = \dfrac{2V}{3L}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2V}{3L}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A closed conducting coil of resistance $10\text{ }\Omega$ is placed in a magnetic field. The magnetic flux linked with the coil varies with time $t$ as $\phi = 3t^2 + 2t + 1\text{ Wb}$. The magnitude of the total charge that flows through the coil during the time interval from $t = 0$ to $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
The total charge $\Delta q$ that flows through a coil of resistance $R$ due to a change in magnetic flux $\Delta \phi$ is given by:
$\Delta q = \dfrac{|\Delta \phi|}{R}$

First, calculate the magnetic flux at the initial and final times:
At $t = 0$, $\phi_1 = 3(0)^2 + 2(0) + 1 = 1\text{ Wb}$
At $t = 2\text{ s}$, $\phi_2 = 3(2)^2 + 2(2) + 1 = 12 + 4 + 1 = 17\text{ Wb}$

The change in magnetic flux is:
$|\Delta \phi| = |17 - 1| = 16\text{ Wb}$

The total charge flown is:
$\Delta q = \dfrac{16}{10} = 1.6\text{ C}$

Using the instantaneous emf at $t = 2\text{ s}$ or forgetting to divide by the resistance leads to incorrect values.

Answer: $1.6\text{ C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A stationary conducting loop of resistance $R$ is placed in a time-varying magnetic field $B(t)$ perpendicular to its plane. Match the time dependence of the magnetic field in List-I with the corresponding qualitative behaviour of the electrical power $P(t)$ dissipated in the loop in List-II.

List-I ($B(t)$)List-II ($P(t)$)
(A) $B(t) = k t$(I) $P(t)$ is constant
(B) $B(t) = k t^2$(II) $P(t)$ is proportional to $t^2$
(C) $B(t) = B_0 \sin(\omega t)$(III) $P(t)$ oscillates between zero and a maximum
(D) $B(t) = B_0 e^{-\alpha t}$(IV) $P(t)$ decreases exponentially

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux through the stationary loop of area $A$ is $\Phi = B(t) A$.
According to Faraday's law, the induced EMF is $\varepsilon = -\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt} = -A \dfrac{dB}{dt}$.
The power dissipated is $P(t) = \dfrac{\varepsilon^2}{R} = \dfrac{A^2}{R} \left( \dfrac{dB}{dt} \right)^2$.

(A) $B(t) = k t \implies \dfrac{dB}{dt} = k$. Thus, $P(t) \propto k^2$, which is a constant. Matches (I).

(B) $B(t) = k t^2 \implies \dfrac{dB}{dt} = 2kt$. Thus, $P(t) \propto (2kt)^2 \propto t^2$. Matches (II).

(C) $B(t) = B_0 \sin(\omega t) \implies \dfrac{dB}{dt} = B_0 \omega \cos(\omega t)$. Thus, $P(t) \propto \cos^2(\omega t)$, which oscillates between zero and a maximum. Matches (III).

(D) $B(t) = B_0 e^{-\alpha t} \implies \dfrac{dB}{dt} = -B_0 \alpha e^{-\alpha t}$. Thus, $P(t) \propto e^{-2\alpha t}$, which decreases exponentially. Matches (IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A square wave voltage that abruptly alternates between $+5\text{ V}$ and $-5\text{ V}$ is considered an alternating EMF.
Reason (R): An alternating EMF must periodically and continuously change its magnitude and reverse its direction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
The Assertion is correct because a square wave that alternates between $+5\text{ V}$ and $-5\text{ V}$ periodically reverses its polarity, which is the essential requirement for an alternating EMF.

The Reason is incorrect because an alternating EMF does not need to change its magnitude continuously. In a square wave, the magnitude remains constant during each half-cycle and changes abruptly, yet it is still a valid alternating EMF.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular coil of $100$ turns, each having an effective area of $0.05\text{ m}^2$, is placed in a uniform magnetic field of $0.4\text{ T}$. If the plane of the coil makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the direction of the magnetic field, the total magnetic flux linked with the coil is:
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux linked with a coil of $N$ turns is given by $\Phi = NBA \cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the area vector (normal to the plane) and the magnetic field.

Given that the plane of the coil makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the magnetic field, the angle with the normal is:
$\theta = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$

Substituting the given values:
$N = 100$
$B = 0.4\text{ T}$
$A = 0.05\text{ m}^2$

$\Phi = 100 \times 0.4 \times 0.05 \times \cos 60^\circ$
$\Phi = 2 \times 0.5 = 1.0\text{ Wb}$

Answer: $1.0\text{ Wb}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The variation of magnetic flux $\phi$ linked with a coil with time $t$ is described as follows: the flux increases linearly from $0$ to $10\text{ Wb}$ in the time interval $t=0$ to $t=2\text{ s}$. It then remains constant at $10\text{ Wb}$ from $t=2\text{ s}$ to $t=4\text{ s}$, and finally decreases linearly to zero from $t=4\text{ s}$ to $t=5\text{ s}$. The ratio of the magnitude of induced emf in the coil during the interval $t=0$ to $2\text{ s}$ to that during the interval $t=4\text{ s}$ to $5\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the magnitude of the induced emf is given by $|e| = \left| \dfrac{\Delta \phi}{\Delta t} \right|$, which represents the absolute value of the slope of the flux-time graph.

For the first interval ($t=0$ to $t=2\text{ s}$):
Initial flux, $\phi_1 = 0$
Final flux, $\phi_2 = 10\text{ Wb}$
Magnitude of induced emf, $|e_1| = \left| \dfrac{10 - 0}{2 - 0} \right| = 5\text{ V}$

For the third interval ($t=4\text{ s}$ to $t=5\text{ s}$):
Initial flux, $\phi_1 = 10\text{ Wb}$
Final flux, $\phi_2 = 0$
Magnitude of induced emf, $|e_2| = \left| \dfrac{0 - 10}{5 - 4} \right| = 10\text{ V}$

The required ratio is $|e_1| : |e_2| = 5 : 10 = 1:2$.

Answer: $1:2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A main circuit branch PQ carries a constant current $i_1 = 2 \text{ A}$ from P to Q. The branch contains a resistor of $5 \ \Omega$ and a primary coil of self-inductance $4 \text{ H}$. A secondary coil is magnetically coupled to the primary coil with a mutual inductance of $3 \text{ H}$. If the current $i_2$ in the secondary coil is increasing at a rate of $2 \text{ A/s}$ and the resulting mutually induced emf opposes the current $i_1$ in the primary coil, what is the potential difference $V_P - V_Q$?
questions.solution:
Apply Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) from P to Q.

The current $i_1$ is constant, so the self-induced emf in the primary coil is zero ($L\dfrac{di_1}{dt} = 0$).

The mutually induced emf in the primary coil due to the changing current in the secondary coil is $E_M = M\dfrac{di_2}{dt} = 3 \times 2 = 6 \text{ V}$.

Since this induced emf opposes the current $i_1$ (which flows from P to Q), it acts as a potential drop when traversing from P to Q.

The potential drop across the resistor is $i_1 R = 2 \times 5 = 10 \text{ V}$.

The KVL equation is:
$V_P - i_1 R - E_M = V_Q$

$V_P - V_Q = i_1 R + E_M = 10 + 6 = 16 \text{ V}$.

Answer: $16 \text{ V}$

questions.q:
Two ideal inductors of inductances $L_1$ and $L_2$ are connected in parallel. A time-varying current flows into this parallel combination. If the rate of change of current in the first inductor is $x$ and the rate of change of current in the second inductor is $y$, and it is given that the ratio $x/y = 3$, what is the ratio of their inductances $L_1/L_2$?
(Neglect mutual inductance)
questions.solution:
For inductors connected in parallel, the potential difference (induced emf) across each branch must be identical.

The induced emf across an inductor is given by $E = L \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.

Therefore, we can write:
$E_1 = E_2$
$L_1 \left(\dfrac{di_1}{dt}\right) = L_2 \left(\dfrac{di_2}{dt}\right)$

Given that the rate of change of current in the first inductor is $x$ and in the second is $y$, we substitute these values:
$L_1 x = L_2 y$

Rearranging to find the ratio of inductances:
$\dfrac{L_1}{L_2} = \dfrac{y}{x}$

Since we are given $x/y = 3$, the inverse ratio is:
$\dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Thus, $\dfrac{L_1}{L_2} = 1/3$.

Answer: $1/3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two solenoidal coils, $P$ and $Q$, are connected in different circuits. Coil $Q$ is wound with twice the total number of turns as coil $P$, has twice the length, and half the cross-sectional area of coil $P$. If the current flowing through coil $Q$ is twice that in coil $P$, the ratio of the magnetic energy stored in coil $P$ to that in coil $Q$ ($U_P : U_Q$) is
questions.solution:
The self-inductance of a solenoid is given by $L = \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l}$.

Let the parameters for coil $P$ be $N_P$, $l_P$, and $A_P$.
For coil $Q$, we are given $N_Q = 2N_P$, $l_Q = 2l_P$, and $A_Q = \dfrac{A_P}{2}$.

The ratio of their self-inductances is:
$\dfrac{L_Q}{L_P} = \left(\dfrac{N_Q}{N_P}\right)^2 \times \left(\dfrac{A_Q}{A_P}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{l_P}{l_Q}\right)$

$\dfrac{L_Q}{L_P} = (2)^2 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{4} = 1$

Thus, $L_P = L_Q$.

The magnetic energy stored in an inductor is $U = \dfrac{1}{2} L i^2$.
Since $L$ is the same for both coils, $U \propto i^2$.

Given that $i_Q = 2i_P$, the ratio of stored energy is:
$\dfrac{U_P}{U_Q} = \left(\dfrac{i_P}{i_Q}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Therefore, the ratio $U_P : U_Q$ is $1:4$.

Answer: $1:4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnitude of the induced emf in a conducting coil varies with time $t$ as $e = 6t + 4 \text{ V}$. The magnitude of the change in magnetic flux linked with the coil between $t = 1 \text{ s}$ and $t = 3 \text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the magnitude of induced emf is given by:
$e = \left| \dfrac{d\phi}{dt} \right|$

The magnitude of the change in magnetic flux is the integral of the emf over the given time interval:
$|\Delta\phi| = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} e \, dt$

Given $e = 6t + 4$, we integrate from $t = 1 \text{ s}$ to $t = 3 \text{ s}$:
$|\Delta\phi| = \int_{1}^{3} (6t + 4) \, dt$
$|\Delta\phi| = \left[ 3t^2 + 4t \right]_{1}^{3}$
$|\Delta\phi| = (3(3)^2 + 4(3)) - (3(1)^2 + 4(1))$
$|\Delta\phi| = (27 + 12) - (3 + 4)$
$|\Delta\phi| = 39 - 7 = 32 \text{ Wb}$

Answer: $32 \text{ Wb}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A conducting loop of resistance $R$ is placed in a uniform, constant magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to its plane. The area of the loop is continuously increased from an initial value $A_0$ at $t=0$ in such a way that the electrical power dissipated in the loop remains a constant value $P_0$. Which of the following expressions represents the area of the loop as a function of time $t$?
questions.solution:
The power dissipated in the loop is given by $P = \dfrac{\varepsilon^2}{R}$, where $\varepsilon$ is the induced EMF.

Given that the power is a constant $P_0$, we have:
$P_0 = \dfrac{\varepsilon^2}{R} \implies |\varepsilon| = \sqrt{P_0 R}$

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the magnitude of the induced EMF is:
$|\varepsilon| = \left| \dfrac{d\Phi}{dt} \right| = B \dfrac{dA}{dt}$ (since $B$ is constant and perpendicular to the loop)

Equating the two expressions for $|\varepsilon|$:
$B \dfrac{dA}{dt} = \sqrt{P_0 R} \implies \dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{P_0 R}}{B}$

Integrating with respect to time $t$, with the initial condition $A(0) = A_0$:
$\int_{A_0}^{A} dA = \int_{0}^{t} \dfrac{\sqrt{P_0 R}}{B} dt$
$A(t) - A_0 = \dfrac{\sqrt{P_0 R}}{B} t$
$A(t) = A_0 + \dfrac{\sqrt{P_0 R}}{B} t$

Answer: $A(t) = A_0 + \dfrac{\sqrt{P_0 R}}{B} t$

questions.q: For a toroid $N=500$, radius $=40 \mathrm{~cm}$, and area of cross section $=10 \mathrm{~cm}^2$. Find inductance.
questions.solution:
If we flow a current $i$, then
$\begin{aligned} & \phi_{\text{self }}=(B \times A) \times N=\left(\frac{\mu_0 N i}{2 \pi R}\right) A \times N \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \phi_{\text{self }}=\left(\frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{2 \pi R}\right) i \text{$ and $} \phi_{\text{self }}=L i\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & L=\frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{2 \pi R}=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{2 N^2 A}{R} \\ & \Rightarrow L=\left(10^{-7}\right) \times \frac{2 \times(500)^2 \times 10 \times\left(10^{-2}\right)^2}{0.4} \\ &=125 \mu \mathrm{H}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform coil of self-inductance $1.8 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{H}$ and resistance $6 \Omega$ is broken up into two identical coils. These two coils are then connected in parallel across a $12 \mathrm{~V}$ battery. The circuit time constant and steady state current through the battery respectively are
questions.solution:
When coil is broken into two identical parts, then resistance of each part
$R^{\prime}=\frac{R}{2}=\frac{6}{2}=3 \Omega$
Inductance of each part
$L^{\prime}=\frac{L}{2}=\frac{1.8}{2} \times 10^{-4}=0.9 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{H}$
Now, time constant $\tau=\frac{L^{\prime}}{R^{\prime}}$
$\tau=\frac{L}{2 \times \frac{R}{2}}=\frac{L}{R}=\frac{1.8 \times 10^{-4}}{6}=30 \mu \mathrm{s}$
Now, effective resistance when both coils are connected in parallel
$R^{\prime \prime}=\frac{R^{\prime} \times R^{\prime}}{R^{\prime}+R^{\prime}}=\frac{3 \times 3}{3+3}=\frac{9}{6} \Omega$
So, maximum current drawn from battery
$I=\frac{V}{R^{\prime \prime}}=\frac{12}{9 / 6}=8 \mathrm{~A}$

questions.q: As shown in figure, two vertical conducting rails separated by distance $1.0 \mathrm{~m}$ are placed parallel to $z$-axis. At $z=0$, a capacitor of $0.15 \mathrm{~F}$ is connected between the rails and a metal rod of mass $100 \mathrm{gm}$ placed across the rails slides down along the rails. If a constant magnetic fields of $2.0 \mathrm{~T}$ exists perpendicular to the plane of the rails, what is the acceleration of the rod? (Take $g=9.8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
Due to motion of rod, emf induced across capacitor, $\varepsilon=B l v \therefore \quad$ Charge stored in capacitor, $Q=C(B l v) I=\frac{d Q}{d t}=C B l \frac{d v}{d t}=C B l a$
Force opposing the downward motion, $F_m=B I l \therefore \quad F_m=B(C B l a) l=B^2 l^2 C a$
Net force on rod, $F_{\text{net }}=W-F_m=m g-B^2 l^2 C a \therefore \quad m a=m g-B^2 l^2 C a$
or $\quad a=\frac{m g}{\left(m+B^2 l^2 C\right)}$
So, $\quad a=\frac{0.1 \times 9.8}{\left(0.1+2^2 \times 1^2 \times 0.15\right)}=1.4 \mathrm{ m} / $$\mathrm{s}^2$

It is rotated about its vertical diameter through $180^{\circ}$ in $0.25 \mathrm{~s}$. The current induced in the coil is (Horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field at that place is $3.0 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~T}$ )
questions.solution:
Initial magnetic flux through the coil,
$\begin{aligned} \phi_i & =B_H A \cos \theta=3.0 \times 10^{-5} \times\left(\pi \times 10^{-2}\right) \times \cos 0^{\circ} \\ & =3 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~Wb}\end{aligned}$
Final magnetic flux after the rotation
$\begin{aligned} \phi_f & =3.0 \times 10^{-5} \times\left(\pi \times 10^{-2}\right) \times \cos 180^{\circ} \\ & =-3 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~Wb}\end{aligned}$
Induced emf, $\varepsilon=-N \frac{d \phi}{d t}=-\frac{N\left(\phi_f-\phi_i\right)}{t} \begin{aligned} & =-\frac{500\left(-3 \pi \times 10^{-2}-3 \pi \times 10^{-7}\right)}{0.25} \\ & =\frac{500 \times\left(6 \pi \times 10^{-7}\right)}{0.25}=3.8 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~V} \\ & I=\frac{\varepsilon}{R}=\frac{3.8 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~V}}{2 \Omega}=1.9 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A circular coil with a cross-sectional area of $4 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ has 10 turns. It is placed at the center of a long solenoid that has 15 turns $/ \mathrm{cm}$ and a crosssectional area of $10 \mathrm{~cm}^2$, as shown in the figure. The axis of the coil conicides with the axis of the solenoid. What is their mutual inductance?
questions.solution:
Let us refer to the coil as circuit 1 and the solenoid as circuit 2 . The field in the central region of the solenoid is uniform, so the flux through the coil is

\Phi_{12}=B_2 A_1=$\left(\mu_$0 n_2 I_2\right) A_1

where $n_2=N_2 / l=1500$ turns $/ \mathrm{m}$. The mutual inductance is

$\begin{aligned}$& M=$\frac{N_1 \Phi_{12}}{I_2}=\mu_$0 n_2 N_1 A_1 \\
& =$\left($4 $\pi \times$10^{-7} $\mathrm{~T} \cdot \mathrm{m}$/ $\mathrm{A}\right)\left($1500 $\mathrm{~m}^{-1}\right)($10)$\left($4 $\times$10^{-4} $\mathrm{~m}^$2\right) \\
& \quad=7.54 $\times$10^{-6} $\mathrm{H}
\end{aligned}$

& \text{$ or $} M=\frac{(1000 \mathrm{ V})(0.01 \mathrm{ s})}{(2 \mathrm{ A})}=5 \mathrm{H} .
\end{aligned}\)$

questions.q: A conducting ring of radius 1 meter is placed in a uniform magnetic field $B$ of 0.01 tesla oscillating with frequency $100 \mathrm{~Hz}$ with its plane at right angle to $B$. What will be the induced electric field?
questions.solution: As a constant magnetic field conducting ring oscillates with a frequency of $100 \mathrm{~Hz}$. i.e. $T=\frac{1}{100} \mathrm{~s}$, for $\frac{T}{2}$, it goes up to $B\therefore$ The corresponding frequency is $200 \mathrm{~Hz}$. $\begin{aligned}$& $\text{ Induced emf }=\frac{\text{ change$ in $flux }}{\text{ time }}$\\ & =$\frac{2 B A \cos \theta}{T}=$2 B A f \cos $\theta$\\ & =$\pi$r^2 $\times$2 $\times$0.01 $\times$200 $\text{ as }$r=1 $\mathrm{~m}$\\ & =$\pi$1^2 $\times$2 $\times$0.01 $\times$200=4 $\pi \mathrm{V} . \end{aligned}$ \\ Non-electrostatic induced electric field along the circle, E=$\frac{1}{2 \pi r} \times\left(\pi$r^2 $\times \frac{d B}{d t}\right)=\frac{e}{2 \pi r}=\frac{4 \pi}{2 \pi r}=$2 $\mathrm{~V}$/ $\mathrm{m} .$
questions.question: A conducting ring of radius 1 meter is placed in a uniform magnetic field $B$ of 0.01 tesla oscillating with frequency $100 \mathrm{~Hz}$ with its plane at right angle to $B$. What will be the induced electric field?
questions.explanation:
As a constant magnetic field conducting ring oscillates with a frequency of $100 \mathrm{~Hz}$. i.e. $T=\frac{1}{100} \mathrm{~s}$, for $\frac{T}{2}$, it goes up to $B \therefore$ The corresponding frequency is $200 \mathrm{~Hz}$. $$ \begin{aligned} & \text{ Induced emf }=\frac{\text{ change in flux }}{\text{ time }} \\ & =\frac{2 B A \cos \theta}{T}=2 B A f \cos \theta \\ & =\pi r^2 \times 2 \times 0.01 \times 200 \text{ as } r=1 \mathrm{~m} \\ & =\pi 1^2 \times 2 \times 0.01 \times 200=4 \pi \mathrm{V} . \end{aligned} $$
Non-electrostatic induced electric field along the circle, $$ E=\frac{1}{2 \pi r} \times\left(\pi r^2 \times \frac{d B}{d t}\right)=\frac{e}{2 \pi r}=\frac{4 \pi}{2 \pi r}=2 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{m} . $$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an ideal parallel $L C$ circuit, the capacitor is charged by connecting it to a d.c. source which is then disconnected. The current in the circuit
questions.solution: When the capacitor is connected to a d.c. source and then disconnected, it gets charged and then it starts discharging through the inductor. An induced emf is produced in the circuit which opposes the growth of current in $L$. When the capacitor is fully discharged, the electric energy stored in the capacitor (i.e. $1 / 2 q^{2 / C}$ ) gets converted fully into magnetic field energy $\left(1 / 2 L I^2\right)$. As soon as the discharge of the capacitor is complete, current stops and the magnetic flux linked with $L$ starts collapsing. Therefore, an induced emf is again developed which starts recharging the capacitor in the opposite direction. When the recharging is completed, all magnetic energy stored in $L$ appears as the electric energy between the plates of the capacitor. The entire process keeps on repeating and the energy taken from the cell keeps on oscillating between $C and L$. Hence the current in the circuit starts oscillating as soon as the d.c. source charging the capacitor is disconnected.

questions.q: For a battery the electromotive force is 1.5 V . Terminal voltage is 1.25 V . Power supplied to external resistance is 2.5 W . Find the internal resistance of battery.
questions.solution:
EMF of battery, $\mathrm{E}=1.5 \mathrm{~V}$
Terminal voltage, $\mathrm{V}=1.25 \mathrm{~V}$
Power supplied to external resistance (R),
i.e. 
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{P} & =2.5 \mathrm{~W} \\
\mathrm{P} & =\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{\mathrm{R}} \\
2.5 & =\frac{(1.25)^2}{\mathrm{R}}
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{R}=\frac{1.25 \times 1.25}{2.5} \\
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{R}=0.625 \Omega
\end{array}$
When battery is used to supply the power to load resistance, then $\mathrm{V}=\mathrm{E}-\mathrm{Ir}$
$\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow V & =E-\left(\frac{V}{R}\right) \cdot r \Rightarrow r=\left(\frac{E}{V}-1\right) R=\left(\frac{1.5}{1.25}-1\right) 0.625 \\
& =0.125 \Omega
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In the given figure what will be the coefficient of mutual inductance
questions.solution: Magnetic field due to wire $\begin{aligned} B & =\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi x} \cdot i \\ d A & =a d x\end{aligned}$ and $\quad d \phi=B \cdot d A$ On integrating both sides, $\begin{aligned} \int d \phi & =\int B d A \\ \phi & =\frac{\mu_0 i}{2 \pi} \int_b^{a+b} \frac{a d x}{x} \\ & =\left.\frac{\mu_0 i}{2 \pi} a \ln x\right|_b ^{a+b} \\ & =\frac{\mu_0 i}{2 \pi} a[\ln (a+b)-\ln b] \\ & =\frac{\mu_0 i}{2 \pi} a\left[\ln \left(1+\frac{a}{b}\right)\right]=M i\end{aligned}$ where, $M=$ coefficient of mutual inductance $\therefore \quad M=\frac{\mu_0 a}{2 \pi} \ln \left(1+\frac{a}{b}\right)$

questions.q: The magnetic flux through each turn of a coil having 200 turns is given as $\left(t^2-2 t\right) \times 10^{-3}$ Wb , where $t$ is in second. The emf induced in the coil at $t=3 \mathrm{~s}$ is
questions.solution:
Given magnetic flux
$\phi=\left(t^2-2 t\right) \times 10^{-3}$
On differentiating with recpect to time $t \frac{d \phi}{d t}=(2 t-2) \times 10^{-3}$
At time $\quad t=3 \mathrm{ s} \begin{aligned}\left|\frac{d \phi}{d t}\right|_{t=3 \mathrm{ s}} & =(2 \times 3-2) \times 10^{-3} \\ & =4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ Wb} \mathrm{ s}^{-1} \\ \text{ Now, }|e| & =N\left|\frac{d \phi}{d t}\right| \\ & =200 \times 4 \times 10^{-3} \\ & =800 \times 10^{-3}=0.8 \mathrm{ V}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The thermo emf of a hypothetical thermocouple varies with the temperature $\theta$ of hot junction as $E=a \theta+b \theta^2$ in volts, where the ratio $\frac{a}{b}$ is $700^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. If the cold junction is kept at $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, then the neutral temperature is
options: no neutral temperature is possible for this thermocouple
questions.solution:
$E=a \theta+b \theta^2$ so $\frac{d E}{d \theta}=a+2 b \theta$
For neutral temperature $\theta=\theta_{\mathrm{n}}, \frac{\mathrm{dE}}{\mathrm{d} \theta}=0$
or $a+2 b \theta_n=0$
or $\theta_{\mathrm{n}}=-\mathrm{a} / 2 \mathrm{~b}=-700 / 2=-350^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
As cold junction is at $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ so negative neutral temperature can not be possible.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Induced emf in the coil depends upon
options: rate of change of linked flux
questions.solution:
According to Faraday's law, "the induced emf in a closed loop equals the time rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop".
i.e., $e=-\frac{d \phi_B}{d t}$
Hence, induced emf in a coil depends on rate of change of flux.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The impedance of a circuit, when a resistance $R$ and an inductor of inductance $L$ are connected in series in an AC circuit of frequency $f$, is
questions.solution:
In $L-R$ circuit,
Impedance $Z=\sqrt{R^2+X_L^2}$
Here, $\quad X_L=\omega L=2 \pi f L$
$\therefore \quad Z=\sqrt{R^2+4 \pi^2 f^2 L^2}$

questions.q: A coil of inductance 300 mH and resistance $2 \Omega$ is connected to a source of voltage 2 V . The current reaches half of its steady state value in
questions.solution: The current at any instant is given by $I=I_0\left(1-e^{-R t / L}\right) \begin{aligned} \frac{I_0}{2} & =I_0\left(1-e^{-R t / L}\right) \\ \frac{1}{2} & =\left(1-e^{-R t / L}\right) \\ e^{-R t / L} & =1 / 2 \\ \frac{R t}{L} & =\ln 2\end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad t=\frac{L}{R} \ln 2 & =\frac{300 \times 10^{-3}}{2} \times 0.693 \\ & =150 \times 0.693 \times 10^{-3} \\ & =0.10395 \mathrm{~s}=0.1 \mathrm{~s} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular coil of mean radius of 7 cm and having 4000 turns is rotated at the rate of 1800 revolutions per minute in the earth's magnetic field $(B=0.5$ gauss), the emf induced in coil will be
questions.solution:
Here: $n=4000, B=0.5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2$
Rate of rotation of coil $=1800 \mathrm{rev} / \mathrm{min}$ =$\frac{1800}{60}=$30 $\mathrm{rev}$ / $\mathrm{sec}$ \begin{aligned} & \omega=2 \pi f=2 \pi \times 30=60 \pi $\mathrm{rad}$ / $\mathrm{s}$, \\ & r=7 $\mathrm{~cm}=$0.07 $\mathrm{~m}$\end{aligned}$
Now area of coil
$A=\pi r^2=\pi \times(0.07)^2=49 \pi \times 10^{-4} $\mathrm{~m}^2$
Now the maximum energy induced is
$\begin{aligned}e & =B A n \omega \\& =0.5 \times 10^{-4} \times 49 \pi \times 10^{-4} \times 4000 \times 60 \pi \\& =0.58 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the current 3 A flowing in the primary coil is made zero in 0.1 sec, the emf induced in the secondary coil is 1.5 volt. The mutual inductance between the coils is
questions.solution:
Here: $e=1.5$ volt
$\Delta i=0-3=-3 \mathrm{~A}, \Delta t=0.1 \mathrm{sec}$
Now the emf induced in secondary coil
$e=\frac{M \Delta i}{\Delta t} \quad$ (numerically)
or $\quad 1.5=\frac{M \times 3}{0.1}$
or $\quad M=\frac{1.5 \times 0.1}{3}=0.05 \mathrm{H}$
